disclaimer: Reminder reference only — NOT legal authority. Season dates are set annually by the Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks and can change. Always verify current regulations with KDWP before hunting or trapping.

license_summary.general: A Kansas furharvester license is required to hunt, trap, or run furbearers. It is unlawful to sell, ship, or offer for sale or shipment any furbearer's hides, pelts, or furs without a trapping/furharvester license for the current calendar year. Nonresidents may hunt/trap only with a nonresident furharvester license. A landowner (and immediate family domiciled with him) may hunt furbearers on his own land by legal methods without a license; tenants have the same privilege on leased agricultural land. (Per K.A.R. 115-5-1 and Kansas regulations summary.)
license_summary.season_times: Per the KDWP 'When to Hunt' page: all furbearer hunting, trapping, and running seasons begin at 12:00 a.m. on opening day and close at midnight of closing day.

sources.notes: Season framework: general furbearer hunting/trapping season from the first Wednesday after the second Saturday in November through February 15; beaver through March 31; otter through March 31, managed by 13 otter management units with unit bag limits of 1-10 otters per trapper and no statewide season quota (per KDWP commission action and the KDWP otter pelt tagging reports: Lower Neosho and Marais des Cygnes units 10; Missouri and Verdigris units 5; Upper Neosho, Kansas, Big Blue, and Lower Arkansas units 2; Middle Arkansas, Republican, Smoky Saline, Solomon, and Western units 1); running season March 1-November 1. Opening time changed to 12:00 a.m. per the KDWP season page. Official code text published by the Kansas Secretary of State. The 115-25-11 text structure (seasons beginning first Wednesday after the second Saturday in November; running season Mar 1-Nov 1) also appears verbatim in the 2011 Wildlife and Parks Commission proposed-regulation record filed with the Kansas Legislature.
sources.title: Kansas Administrative Regulations — official K.A.R. publications (Kansas Secretary of State)

sources.notes: Legal equipment, taking methods, and coyote provisions: coyote is NOT classified as a furbearer in Kansas; artificial light/thermal/night-vision equipment for hunting coyotes Jan 1 - Mar 31 requires a department permit. verification.confirmation_notes: Data built from Kansas statutory/regulatory framework: K.A.R. 115-25-11 season structure (general furbearer hunting/trapping season from the first Wednesday after the second Saturday in November through February 15; beaver through March 31; otter through March 31 managed by 13 otter management units with unit bag limits of 1-10 otters per trapper and no statewide season quota), the KDWP 'When to Hunt' page (12:00 a.m. opening / midnight closing times), the official KDWP 2024-25 Furharvester Activity Survey (extended year-round raccoon/opossum hunting and trapping season), and K.A.R. 115-5-1 (coyote not a furbearer; thermal/night-vision coyote permit rules). 2026-27 dates computed from the regulatory formula: first Wednesday after the second Saturday in November 2026 = November 18, 2026 (verified with date -d). Code citations (K.A.R. 115-25-11 and 115-5-1) now point to the official Kansas Secretary of State K.A.R. publications instead of the Cornell LII mirror. Season opening dates computed from the 115-25-11 formula: first Wednesday after the second Saturday in November 2026 = Nov 18, 2026 (Wednesday), verified with date -d.
known_gaps: 2026-27 raccoon/opossum extended season: confirmed as policy from the 2024-25 KDWP survey ('new' in 2024-25); presumed continuing for 2026-27. If KDWP ended the extension, hunting/trapping revert to the Nov 18-Feb 15 regular season only.

Otter unit bag limits are per K.A.R. 115-25-11 as amended and the KDWP 2024-25 otter pelt tagging report (10 in Lower Neosho and Marais des Cygnes units; 5 in Missouri and Verdigris units; 2 in Upper Neosho, Kansas, Big Blue, and Lower Arkansas units; 1 in Middle Arkansas, Republican, Smoky Saline, Solomon, and Western units). Re-verify unit boundaries and bag limits against current KDWP notices before trapping.
Firearms deer season dates (which close coyote hunting) were not verified for 2026.
Bobcat/swift fox/otter pelt-tagging requirements are per KDWP harvest-monitoring programs; confirm current tagging station/contact requirements with KDWP.
Specific equipment limitations during the extended (off-regular-season) raccoon/opossum trapping period were not verified — verify with KDWP.
Scientific names are standard taxonomy, not stated in Kansas sources.
Running seasons (March 1 - November 1 for bobcat, gray/red fox; raccoon/opossum running now folded into the extended hunting season) are non-take seasons and not modeled.
Fees and exact license product names were not verified and are omitted.

Western Kansas (roughly west of the I-83 corridor — Sherman, Wallace, Greeley, Hamilton, Stanton, Morton, Stevens, Meade, Seward and adjacent counties) observes Mountain Time; the dataset uses America/Chicago statewide — adjust clock-dependent times for Mountain-Time counties. All K.A.R. 115-25-11 season boundary times are 12:00 midnight/midnight boundaries.
